sources.shortCitation: Musée SACEM, creator record for Léo Lelièvre (fils)
sources.fullCitation: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique. “Léo Lelièvre (fils).” Musée SACEM, Les créateurs. Born 9 June 1899 in Paris, died 21 June 1966 in Prague; admitted to SACEM as author on 13 November 1919 and as composer on 21 April 1927, elected full member in 1927; Prix Ferny, 1939.
sources.title: Léo Lelièvre (fils)
sources.creator: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique
sources.repository: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique
sources.researchNote: The society through which both men licensed their work distinguishes the son by the qualifier “fils” and dates his membership from 1919, ten years before the first Casino de Paris covers that carry that qualifier. The place of death, Prague, is recorded here alone among the authority files consulted.

sources.shortCitation: Musée SACEM, creator record for Jean Féline
sources.fullCitation: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique. “Jean Féline.” Musée SACEM, Les créateurs. Lyricist, screenwriter and dialogue writer, born 30 October 1908 in Saumur, died 17 January 1945 in Paris; admitted to SACEM as author on 1 May 1935.
sources.title: Jean Féline
sources.creator: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique
sources.repository: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique
sources.researchNote: The membership register gives 30 October 1908 as the date of birth, agreeing with the Paris death certificate of January 1945 and superseding the tentative year 1912 carried by the BnF heading. Admission as an author on 1 May 1935 marks the start of his professional song writing, shortly before the first songs published under his name.

sources.shortCitation: Musée SACEM, identity photograph of Jacques Monteux
sources.fullCitation: “Photo d’identité de Jacques Monteux.” Photographic print, 4.5 × 3.7 cm, from the membership file of the sociétaire Jacques Monteux. Document d’archives Sacem, Musée SACEM. © Fonds Sacem.
sources.title: Photo d’identité de Jacques Monteux
sources.creator: Photographer unidentified
sources.repository: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique
sources.researchNote: The museum records neither photographer nor date, only the support and the size of the print. The name written across the image, “Monteux Jacques Jacob”, supplies the given names that the authority headings omit. The sitter appears to be in his twenties, which agrees with the application for membership of March 1926 preserved in the same file.

sources.shortCitation: Musée SACEM, creator record for Jacques Monteux
sources.fullCitation: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique. “Jacques Monteux.” Musée SACEM, Les créateurs. Dialogue writer and lyricist, born in Paris on 5 November 1899, died 7 April 1979; admitted to SACEM on 2 March 1926 and elected full member on 8 April 1933.
sources.title: Jacques Monteux
sources.creator: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique
sources.repository: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique
sources.researchNote: The biography spells the surname “Monteaux” while the heading of the same record, the membership photograph and the authority files read Monteux. The dates of birth and death agree with the authority files to the day. Admission on 2 March 1926 places the start of his registered authorship seven years before the two Kaper and Jurmann songs he wrote for the French version of “Madame ne veut pas d’enfants”.

sources.shortCitation: Musée SACEM, creator record for Henri Varna
sources.fullCitation: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique. “Henri Varna.” Musée SACEM, Les créateurs. Author, born in Marseille on 31 October 1887, died in Paris on 10 April 1969; elected full member of SACEM on 30 August 1918.
sources.title: Henri Varna
sources.researchNote: The membership register places his admission to the society in 1918, nine years before he took over the direction of the Casino de Paris, and gives his birth and death to the day.

sources.shortCitation: Musée SACEM, creator record for André de Badet
sources.fullCitation: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique. “André de Badet.” Musée SACEM, Les créateurs. Author, born at Escos on 30 June 1891, died at Clamart on 7 April 1977; elected full member of SACEM as author on 29 April 1933; Prix Célestin Joubert, 1964.
sources.title: André de Badet
sources.researchNote: The society dates his standing as a full member from April 1933, the season of the French songs he wrote for Kaper and Jurmann, and confirms the places of birth and death that the authority heading leaves out.

sources.shortCitation: Musée SACEM, creator record for Louis Poterat
sources.fullCitation: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique. “Louis Poterat.” Musée SACEM, Les créateurs. Author, born at Troyes on 2 June 1901, died at Geneva on 6 January 1982; elected full member of SACEM on 27 April 1928; administrator of SACEM, vice-president and secretary general of the SDRM; Prix Albert Willemetz, 1946.
sources.title: Louis Poterat
sources.researchNote: Besides the dates, the register records the offices he later held in the society and in the mechanical rights body, which no other record consulted for him mentions.

sources.fullCitation: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique. “Marc Cab.” Musée SACEM, Les créateurs. Author, born at Nice on 11 December 1901, died at Bandol on 18 October 1978; admitted to SACEM as author on 21 November 1923; Prix Albert Willemetz, 1949.
sources.title: Marc Cab
sources.researchNote: The society spells the name without a hyphen and supplies the places of birth and death, which the authority heading reduces to years alone.

sources.shortCitation: Musée SACEM, creator record for René Nazelles
sources.fullCitation: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique. “René Nazelles.” Musée SACEM, Les créateurs. Author and composer, born in Paris on 8 October 1888, died on 11 September 1975; elected full member of SACEM on 13 September 1911; Prix Salabert, 1958.
sources.title: René Nazelles
sources.researchNote: The register settles the life dates that the BnF heading still gives as an open span, agreeing with the years recorded by the film and record databases, and dates his standing in the society from 1911.

sources.shortCitation: Musée SACEM, creator record for Charles-Louis Pothier
sources.fullCitation: Société des auteurs, compositeurs et éditeurs de musique. “Charles-Louis Pothier.” Musée SACEM, Les créateurs. Author, born at Bordeaux on 18 April 1881, died at Clichy on 3 November 1962; elected full member of SACEM on 17 February 1912; Prix Trebitsch, 1943; Prix Albert Willemetz, 1947; Prix Centenaire, 1950; Prix Célestin Joubert, 1956; Grand Prix de la Chanson, 1958.
sources.title: Charles-Louis Pothier
sources.researchNote: The list of society prizes, running from 1943 to 1958, documents a standing in the profession that the catalogue records do not show, and the register confirms the places of birth and death.
